reasons: intent_insensitive: question four is no: a different enemy intent would not have changed the line, so the intent is not part of the decision

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Duck and Cover first, then played both Kaboom! cards at Fuzzy Wurm Crawler. Firework Finale and Ka-pow! were not playable because the page says they are blocked by card logic, and the Spark bank is empty.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I considered playing both Kaboom! cards and skipping Duck and Cover, but rejected it because Duck and Cover costs no opportunity cost this turn and blocks the telegraphed 4 damage.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up no known benefit on the page. It spent all available energy and played every playable card, so the only things given up were worse alternatives: taking 4 damage by skipping Duck and Cover, or dealing 7 less damage by skipping one Kaboom!.
answers.q4_different_intent: No. Since all three playable cards fit within 3 energy, a different enemy intent would not create a tradeoff between damage and block. Duck and Cover would still be playable without preventing either Kaboom!, and the two Kaboom! cards would still be playable.

survives_means: not yet falsified -- this funnel refuses turns and never rates them

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
targets.repair: out of scope by M63: this refuses a form and never repairs one

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
